raw_response:
My land is in the North China Plain. I have been farming here for over 50 years. My father farmed this land. His father farmed this land. What we grow here is wheat in the winter and corn in the summer. That is what I will grow again this year.

I have about 7 mu left that I work myself. My youngest son helps me during wheat harvest in June and corn harvest in October. I rented out 3 mu to my neighbor last year because I could not manage it — my back is not good. 7 mu is enough for me.

For the wheat, I will buy Jimai 22 seeds from the village supply cooperative, the same as last year. It gave me a decent harvest. I will rotary-till the field before sowing in October, put down the base fertilizer at sowing time — urea and diammonium phosphate mixed together, the way I always do — then top-dress with urea at jointing. I will water three times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Two pesticide sprays — one herbicide in early spring and one for aphids when they come in May.

For the corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. I will not till — no time and my tractor cost money to run. I buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seeds. I apply fertilizer twice. I water maybe twice if August is dry. One pesticide spray for corn borer if I see them.

I do not grow cotton anymore. Too much bending, too much spraying. My knees cannot do it.
